title: Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual software fee for running agents on AI infrastructure
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing annual software fees of around $2,000 per GPU for enterprise AI, a model that could generate $10 billion a year if five million licenses were sold. The pricing and launch timeline remain unconfirmed, while Nvidia continues to expand its AI software and security tools for enterprise customers.

title: New CD players keep launching, but a drive shortage could make them unfixable
content: The lack of optical drive manufacturers is raising questions about the repairability and longevity of new CD players that are coming out on the market today.

title: AMD CEO Lisa Su proposed bringing back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, set plan in motion before DDR5 shortages
content: AMD Director Travis Kirsch confirmed the rationale for relaunching the first X3D chip and explained why the company no longer offers many Ryzen 3 SKUs.

title: Nvidia eyes converting old nuclear plants into massive AI data centers
content: Nvidia and PreussenElektra are studying whether decommissioned sites of German nuclear power plants can be repurposed as AI data centers, potentially cutting development time by reusing existing grid connections, land, and industrial infrastructure.

title: Nvidia unveils OOI CPO prototype for post-2028 AI needs
content: Nvidia has unveiled a prototype of its next-generation co-packaged optics (CPO) technology, Optics-on-Interposer (OOI), at SEMICON West 2026. The design moves the optical engine from a conventional organic package substrate to the silicon interposer carrying the compute chips, increasing bandwidth density and reducing power consumption for future AI system interconnects.

title: Namuga expands beyond Samsung with humanoid robot camera modules
content: South Korean image-sensing module maker Namuga is accelerating its physical AI strategy after securing a supply deal with a global humanoid robot company. The company is preparing for shipments and mass production while targeting revenue of KRW1 trillion (approximately US$754.7 million) by 2030.

title: AI data centers drive Taiwan's electrical firms into modular, EPC markets
content: As demand for AI data centers expands, next-generation AI servers are raising requirements for power supply, cooling efficiency, and deployment speed. Taiwan's electrical and mechanical equipment providers are therefore moving beyond standalone equipment supply into system integration, engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC), and modular data center solutions.

title: Meta’s AI commitments surge to US$825 billion, testing financing power
content: Meta Platforms’ long-term AI infrastructure spending is driving rising financial pressure, with free cash flow turning negative in Q3 2026 and future lease and non-cancelable contract commitments climbing to about US$825 billion. The company also raised the lower end of its 2026 capex forecast by US$5 billion to US$135 billion, signaling continued AI expansion as financing and investment returns become new challenges.

title: Texas Instruments sees up to $1,000 in chip content per humanoid robot as analog supply tightens
content: Texas Instruments (TI) held its latest earnings call this week, projecting fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of US$5.8 billion to US$6.3 billion. The midpoint of its guidance is broadly in line with third-quarter revenue, outperforming the seasonal declines typically seen in the fourth quarter.

title: Magnate Technology sees aerospace, semiconductor growth opportunities
content: Magnate Technology expects rising aircraft engine demand and semiconductor equipment opportunities to support growth as it expands production capacity, with implications for global aviation and chip supply chains. The aerospace components maker forecasts revenue of nearly NT$2 billion (US$61.5 million) in 2026 and expects 15% to 20% revenue growth in 2027.

title: Exynos 2700 Internal Tests Show Qualcomm’s 2nm And New Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 Packaging Bet Failed; Samsung’s Flagship SoC 20% Faster In CPU, GPU Workloads
content: New details surrounding the Exynos 2700 talk about the chipset’s internal tests allegedly outperforming the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 in both CPU and GPU workloads. The latest claim paints Qualcomm’s top-end SoC in a negative light, indicating that its transition to TSMC’s 2nm node and Offset PoP packaging didn’t help matters. However, we’ve noticed a trend on foreign outlets where the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6’s capabilities are being downplayed, likely to hype up the Exynos 2700.
